strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the 'learning cliff' in RLVR with clear formalization and visualization
Sound technical approach with rigorous on-policy formulation and theoretical analysis showing advantages over off-policy alternatives
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 benchmarks, 5 model architectures, and extensive ablations demonstrating consistent 44.3% relative improvement on AIME24
Thorough ablation studies validating each design choice (exemption period robustness 10-40%, necessity of 3-tier hierarchy, progressive guidance)
Excellent reproducibility with complete hyperparameters, detailed setup, promised code release, and clear presentation
Conservative design that maintains on-policy learning without modifying the GRPO loss, only augmenting training data
Computational efficiency: guidance triggered for only 17.4% of samples, achieves better results (50.9%) in similar time to vanilla GRPO
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: hierarchical hints and scaffolding are established pedagogical concepts; application to RLVR, while sensible, is relatively straightforward
Scalability concerns: requires high-quality teacher model (DeepSeek-R1) for hint generation; unclear if weaker models suffice; limits practical applicability
Narrow domain scope: primarily evaluated on mathematics; generalization to other reasoning tasks (code, logic, language) unclear; GPQA-Diamond OOD results match LUFFY rather than exceed it

Experimental setup issues: data reuse between training and hint generation raises contamination concerns; LUFFY trained on filtered dataset (different setup than original); pass@1 results lack error bars or confidence intervals

Arbitrary methodological choices: 15% exemption period justified only empirically; 3-level hint hierarchy lacks principled justification; hint incremental structure undefined; random trajectory replacement not optimized

Incomplete analysis of core claims: 'skill internalization' (Figure 5 is single example); skill graduation metric vaguely defined; post-training retention untested; claims about genuine capability gain vs hint-structure overfitting lack rigorous validation
Missing failure case analysis: frequency of intractable problems not reported; statistics on hierarchical search failures absent; no analysis of which problem types benefit most/least

Hint quality dependency inadequately explored: Table 14 shows quality matters but with limited analysis; no degradation curves for weaker hints; scaling to new domains requires generating quality hints

strengths: Identifies and clearly illustrates a real problem (learning cliff in RLVR) with compelling empirical evidence (Figure 2)
Strong empirical results on mathematical benchmarks: 44.3% relative improvement over vanilla GRPO and 9.2% over LUFFY on Qwen2.5-Math-7B
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek), sizes (1.5B-7B), and benchmarks
Thoughtful two-phase design (guidance exemption + hierarchical hints) with pedagogical motivation from scaffolding theory
Maintains on-policy principle with technically correct probability ratio computations; lower clip ratios than off-policy alternatives (Figure 7)
Extensive ablation studies validating component choices; robustness analysis across guidance exemption periods (Table 11)
Excellent supplementary documentation with detailed prompts, algorithms, and implementation details
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: providing hints for difficult problems is well-established in curriculum learning; hierarchical in-prompt hints vs. prefixes is primarily engineering-level variation, not methodological innovation
Confounding variables in experimental design: custom data filtering (Table 3) provides separate 6% benefit to vanilla GRPO; unclear how much improvement comes from scaffolding vs. filtering strategy

Critical dependency on external teacher model: 4% performance drop with lower-quality hints (Table 14); hint generation requires DeepSeek-R1 and careful prompt engineering; significant reproducibility and scalability concerns

Overstated on-policy claim: batch Gfinal contains trajectories from different prompt distributions π(·|q) vs π(·|q⊕h*); this is inherently off-policy despite correct probability ratio computation; Appendix F.5 defense is circular
Insufficient statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; single-run results concerning for LLM evaluation; no significance testing on reported improvements

Limited generalization evidence: math-only evaluation; OOD benchmark (GPQA-Diamond) shows Scaf-GRPO ties LUFFY (37.3%), not exceeding; 15.5% OOD gain vs 44.3% in-domain gain suggests in-distribution fitting rather than robust skill learning

Heuristic guidance exemption period detection: 'rate of solving zero-reward queries plateaus' lacks precise definition; 15% hyperparameter appears arbitrary despite Table 11 showing robustness across 10-40%

Incomplete prefix method comparison: distributed mismatch critique unsupported; LUFFY's policy shaping designed for this; no fair ablation comparing identical guidance mechanisms; 9.2% improvement is modest given added complexity
Computational efficiency overstated: 13h → 12h (~7.7% improvement) is marginal; cost of deterministic hint search not detailed; memory overhead negligible (72→73 GB)
Questionable design choices: random trajectory replacement strategy (line 11, Algorithm 1), 3-tier hierarchy (K-P-S), and 4-item hint levels appear unmotivated; no ablations testing alternatives
Skill graduation metric questionable (Table 4): higher graduations may reflect better optimization of training distribution rather than deeper learning, consistent with weak OOD generalization
Missing essential experiments: no multiple runs for variance estimation, no alternative hint structures tested, no analysis of failure cases or problem-type dependencies

strengths: Well-motivated problem: The 'learning cliff' is clearly articulated with compelling analysis showing how zero-reward signals cause advantage collapse in GRPO
Novel approach superior to prefix-continuation methods: Maintains policy consistency via in-prompt hints rather than forcing predetermined solution paths, avoiding distributional mismatch

Principled two-phase design: Guidance exemption period effectively distinguishes 'true-hard' from 'pseudo-hard' problems; hierarchical Knowledge→Planning→Solution hints encourage skill internalization

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 7 mathematical benchmarks + GPQA-Diamond OOD, multiple architectures (Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek-R1), consistent improvements (44.3% relative on AIME24 vs GRPO; 9.2% over LUFFY)

Rigorous technical analysis: Formal mathematical treatment with clear algorithmic description; comparative on-policy vs off-policy analysis with empirical validation; 'skill graduation' metric provides evidence of genuine capability gains

Excellent ablation studies: Table 2 systematically validates each component; Table 11 demonstrates robustness across 10-40% exemption period range; Appendix F.5 empirically validates on-policy stability
Strong reproducibility: Complete source code promised, detailed hyperparameters, extensive appendices, multiple evaluation metrics (pass@1 and avg@16)
weaknesses: Critical dependence on high-quality hints: Offline generation via DeepSeek-R1 creates non-trivial data preparation overhead; limited evaluation of robustness to hint quality variation; makes scaling to new domains challenging

Strictly limited scope: Method restricted to verifiable solutions and structured reasoning (mathematics only); GPQA-Diamond is OOD but still in scientific domain; unclear applicability to open-ended tasks

Modest OOD generalization: GPQA-Diamond results (37.3%) match LUFFY baseline and show only 15.5% relative improvement over Vanilla GRPO (vs 44.3% on AIME24); raises concerns about hint-specific memorization vs fundamental reasoning gains

Ad-hoc design choices lacking principled justification: 15% exemption period empirically chosen; plateau detection algorithm not precisely specified; data filtering strategy (8 samples per problem) lacks theoretical grounding; random trajectory replacement could introduce variance

Incomplete overhead characterization: Hierarchical 3×4 hint search during training has real cost; time comparison (12h vs 13h) is marginal and excludes hint generation preprocessing; no breakdown of total pipeline costs for practitioners
Insufficient statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; some improvements modest (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B +3.4% absolute); no seed-based variance analysis
Missing failure case analysis: No systematic study of when Scaf-GRPO fails to help; limited exploration of alternative hint hierarchies; unclear which problem categories benefit most

Distributional mismatch argument could be stronger: While empirically validated, theoretical claim that hints fundamentally alter π(·|q) vs π(·|q⊕h*) deserves deeper justification; off-policy alternative (47.3% vs 50.9%) shows non-trivial gap exists
